description:
The Death Benefit under the Odisha Building and Other Construction Workers Welfare Board (O.B.O.C.W.W.B) is a significant welfare scheme initiated by the Government of Odisha.

This scheme was launched to provide financial assistance to the families of construction workers who lose their lives while engaged in work-related activities.

The scheme was officially implemented on 1st January 2008 as part of the broader efforts to enhance the welfare of construction workers in the state.

The primary objective of the Death Benefit scheme is to ensure that the families of deceased workers receive immediate financial support during their time of grief.

The scheme aims to provide a one-time financial assistance of ₹2 lakh to the family of the deceased worker.

This amount is intended to help cover funeral expenses and provide some financial stability to the family during a difficult period.

To be eligible for the Death Benefit, the deceased worker must have been registered with the Odisha Building and Other Construction Workers Welfare Board.

The worker must have been actively engaged in construction work at the time of their death.

There is no specific age limit for the workers under this scheme.

However, it is essential that the worker has made contributions to the welfare fund for a minimum period as specified by the board.

The family of the deceased worker must submit an application for the Death Benefit within a stipulated time frame.

The application must be made within 90 days of the worker's death to ensure timely disbursement of the benefits.

To apply for the Death Benefit, the family members must provide specific documents.

These documents include a copy of the death certificate of the worker.

They must also submit a copy of the worker's registration certificate with the O.B.O.C.W.W.B.

Additionally, the family must provide proof of relationship to the deceased worker.

This can include documents such as a ration card or any government-issued ID that establishes the relationship.

The application form can be obtained from the local office of the Odisha Building and Other Construction Workers Welfare Board.

It can also be downloaded from the official website of the board.

Once the application is filled out and the necessary documents are attached, it must be submitted to the local office.

The local office will then verify the details and process the application.

Upon successful verification, the financial assistance of ₹2 lakh will be disbursed to the eligible family.

The disbursement is typically made through direct bank transfer to the bank account of the beneficiary.

The Odisha Building and Other Construction Workers Welfare Board is the implementing authority for this scheme.

The board operates under the Department of Labour and Employees' State Insurance, Government of Odisha.

The contact details for the Odisha Building and Other Construction Workers Welfare Board can be found on the official government website.

The board also conducts awareness programs to inform construction workers about the benefits available under this scheme.

As of October 2023, the scheme has provided financial assistance to thousands of families across Odisha.

This initiative has significantly alleviated the financial burden on families who have lost their primary breadwinners.

The government has also emphasized the importance of registering construction workers with the board to ensure they can avail themselves of such benefits.

The scheme is part of a larger framework of welfare measures aimed at improving the living conditions of construction workers in Odisha.

The government has been proactive in updating the eligibility criteria and benefits to ensure they meet the needs of the workers.

In addition to the Death Benefit, the Odisha Building and Other Construction Workers Welfare Board offers various other welfare measures.

These include financial assistance for education, health care, and housing for registered workers.

The board has also established a grievance redressal mechanism to address any issues faced by the beneficiaries.

The Death Benefit scheme is a crucial part of the government's commitment to the welfare of workers in the unorganized sector.

The Odisha government has allocated significant funds each year to sustain this welfare scheme.

In the financial year 2022-2023, the government allocated ₹100 crore for the welfare of construction workers.

This allocation reflects the government's ongoing commitment to improving the lives of construction workers and their families.

The scheme has been well-received by the public and has garnered positive feedback from beneficiaries.

Many families have expressed gratitude for the timely support provided by the government during their time of loss.

The government continues to monitor the implementation of the scheme to ensure that it meets its objectives effectively.

Regular audits and assessments are conducted to evaluate the impact of the Death Benefit scheme on the lives of the beneficiaries.

The Odisha Building and Other Construction Workers Welfare Board is also working on enhancing its outreach programs.

These programs aim to educate workers about their rights and the benefits available to them.

The board is committed to ensuring that no worker is left behind and that all eligible families receive the support they need.

The Death Benefit scheme is a testament to the government's dedication to the welfare of its citizens.

It highlights the importance of social security measures in protecting vulnerable populations.

The scheme serves as a model for other states in India to develop similar welfare programs for construction workers.

The government encourages all construction workers to register with the Odisha Building and Other Construction Workers Welfare Board.

This registration is crucial for availing of benefits under the Death Benefit scheme and other welfare initiatives.

The scheme has played a vital role in providing a safety net for families of construction workers in Odisha.

It underscores the importance of social security in promoting the welfare of workers in the unorganized sector.

The Death Benefit scheme is an essential part of Odisha's commitment to improving the lives of its workers.
